title: MCP Server Lifecycle
description: Set up an MCP server project in C#, understand initialization, capability negotiation, and request handling.

blocks.text: An MCP server is a process or service that exposes resources, prompts, and tools using the Model Context Protocol. In C#, you can host it as a console app with stdio, an ASP.NET Core endpoint with HTTP, or a background service in an existing app.

blocks.title: Typical lifecycle
items: **Initialize** - client and server exchange capabilities and protocol versions.
**Register primitives** - server advertises available tools, resources, and prompts.
**Handle requests** - server receives tool calls, resource reads, or prompt invocations.
**Shutdown** - server cleans up resources and exits cleanly.

blocks.text: Create a new console or ASP.NET Core project and add the MCP SDK package. Register tools using attribute-based or fluent registration, then run the server in the desired transport mode.

blocks.title: Conceptual MCP server bootstrap
blocks.content: This sketch shows server setup without binding to a specific SDK version.

blocks.title: Check the current SDK
blocks.text: MCP SDKs for .NET are evolving quickly. Prefer the latest stable package and validate transport support before building production infrastructure.

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: MCP servers can be local or remote depending on transport.
Lifecycle includes initialization, capability exchange, and clean shutdown.
C# hosting models range from simple console apps to full ASP.NET Core services.
blocks.takeaway: Choose the simplest transport that meets your deployment needs, then add HTTP only when you need remote access.
